executionPlan: Reran lint, tests and builds myself on Node 22 (online build and a network-denied build, each in its own copy of the tree). Ran a production server from a copy and drove it with headless Chrome 154 over CDP on the real GPU (Apple M1 Pro, ANGLE Metal; the WebGL renderer string was read back and a SwiftShader control was run separately). Reused the dev harness only as a starting point and wrote my own probes: exit exactness (DOM signature plus whole-frame pixel diff), title and silhouette frame analysis, stale-strip and focus probes, mobile focus probe, font pixel diff against a Google-font build, and a mutation check of the defect fix in a throwaway copy. M1 regression used the round-3 harness re-pointed at the real GPU. Every Chrome launched was closed; one stale browser left by a regression script was killed. All servers I started were stopped; the dev server on 3100 was left running.
summary: Rejected on one reproducible defect: whenever the inline loading strip was shown during Play (any load slower than 400 ms: cold visit, touch device, Retry), the later Exit mounts an invisible strip whose Cancel button steals focus, so focus ends on the page body instead of Play. Everything else I tested passes: lint 0, 348 tests, both builds 0 with / at 125 kB, bundle boundary clean, transition smooth and judged by eye and frame diff, exit exact, failure paths, pause, mic release, cycles, M1 regression and font. The Boss weak spots: the 14 percent title is invisible in practice, and the exit swap itself is invisible (swap pair diff 0.68 vs neighbour median 2.6); the 1.9x pair the dev saw is the last accelerating fov step before the swap, not the swap.

criteria.criterion: The Play transition was recorded (DevTools protocol screencast or per-frame captures at 1440x900 on a real GPU, both warm after hover and cold without hover, at scroll 0 and a scrolled offset) and judged by eye and by frame diff: every page chrome element fades and slides out with a visible stagger, no layout jump, no hard cut, no blank frame, no T-pose or bind-pose frame, no flash of the hero layout, the avatar turns and walks into the world while the camera settles behind, the HUD fades in, input is enabled by about 2 s after click, and rAF frame time p95 is under 20 ms during the transition; the Boss's noted weak spots (title still about 14 percent opaque at C+360, exit swap pose step 1.9x neighbours) are judged visible or invisible with evidence.
criteria.evidence: All four recordings (warm0, cold0, warm300, cold300; Apple M1 Pro real GPU, Chrome 154, 1440x900, production build) reviewed as contact sheets and measured. Chrome fades with visible stagger (status, gestures, nav gone by C+360, title and buttons last), monotonic opacity, section and about rects constant (1 distinct), scrollWidth constant 1430, no blank frames, 0 T-pose rows, ground colour at S matches stage colour. Avatar yaw pi at S, turn complete before S+570, walk 2.17 m by S+1500, camera widens from fov 32 while settling behind, HUD first visible S+1022 and opaque S+1272. Warm input ready at C+1945 to 1947, cold at C+2244 to 2246 (about 2 s, 0.25 s slower cold). rAF p95 17.5 to 17.8 ms in all four runs; exactly one 28 ms frame at the swap per run. Scrolled starts: wrapper slides 300 px smoothly, the page fades 18.9 to 9 brightness over about 250 ms with no snap. Weak spot 1, title at C+360: its brightest pixel falls 182, 91 (C+334), 48 (C+368), 23 (C+384), 7 equals background (C+401), a last step of 16 levels on glyph pixels only; judged invisible. Weak spot 2, exit swap: the swap pair diff is 0.68 against a neighbour median of 2.6 and silhouette bounds are identical across the swap (590 px high before and after), so the swap is invisible; the larger pair (6.56 vs about 2.6, 2.5x in my measure) is the last camera fov step, whose size grows about 7 percent per frame and then stops dead at X+700 because the spec requires ease-in on the exit fov (play-transition.md 4.1). That arrival is a visible but spec-conforming snap; see finding F-M2-2 (low). Files: metrics-*.json, mont-warm0-a.jpg, mont-warm0-b.jpg, mont-swap.jpg, mont-cold0.jpg, mont-cold300.jpg, exit-swap-a.jpg.

DOM signature of all 399 body nodes identical after Exit at scroll 0 and 300 except the typewriter text and caret blink in the hint box; whole-frame pixel diff with canvas hidden and animations frozen is 0 of 1,296,000 px at scroll 300 and 0 px outside the hint box at scroll 0; scrollY restored to 0 and 300; html and body styles clean. Reduced motion crossfades with 0 transform frames and the camera snaps (spec 5). Mobile emulation shows controls fading in and the tap skip reaching fov 55. FAILS: the focus-on-Play requirement does not hold after any Play in which the strip was shown. Reproduction (stalestrip.mjs 900, and mobile.mjs/mfocus.mjs for the touch case): hold the load past 400 ms or use a touch device, enter the game, press Exit; the focus log reads Play focused, then Cancel focused (an invisible strip mounted), then BODY, and the final active element is the body. Hover-warm runs, which the dev harness used, never show the strip and so never hit it. Root cause and fix are in finding F-M2-1; mutation check in a copy with one added line gives active element Play and no strip. Files: stalestrip text output, mfocus3.mjs output, mobile.txt, loading*.txt.

findings.trigger: Play where the inline strip was shown (load not finished at 400 ms: first cold visit, every touch device because touch prefetches code only, or Retry after a failure), then Exit (HUD, pause menu or Escape path through completeReturn).
findings.consequence: swap() calls stripOut() but never clears stripShownAt, so at Exit completeReturn runs stripOut() while stripShownAt is still set, mounts the strip in state out, and LoadingStrip.tsx lines 48-50 move focus to its Cancel button. Focus leaves Play (the focus-on-Play guarantee) and lands on the body when the strip unmounts 150 ms later; keyboard and screen-reader users lose their place. The strip is at opacity 0 so there is no visible flash. Reproduced on desktop and on mobile emulation, and the Retry then Exit path hits it too.
findings.evidence: Focus log after Exit with the unmodified tree: Play focused, then Cancel focused, then body; final active element BODY. Same probe against a throwaway copy with one added line in swap() (stripShownAt.current = null): no strip mounted during Exit, active element Play. The dev harness and the shell tests are all warm or never assert focus after a strip run, so none caught it.
findings.rule: Acceptance criterion: Exit restores focus on Play; play-transition.md 4.4 (focus on Play at X+700). Suggested fix: reset stripShownAt in swap after stripOut, or in completeReturn before calling stripOut; add a shell test that shows the strip, enters, exits and asserts the active element is Play.

assumptions: Real GPU numbers are from the Apple M1 Pro (ANGLE Metal) under headless Chrome 154; the SwiftShader control returned 44 fps idle and was not used for any timing or visual judgement.
Production-build recordings use a next start from a copy of this tree; dev server numbers were used only for the M1 regression, the Retry chunk-name case and the unpatched stale-strip reproduction.

The headless harness injects a store hook and a listener counter; its numbers are the same mechanism as the dev's, but the judgements, the exit-exactness probe, the focus probes and the font comparison are my own.
Mobile results are touch and coarse-pointer emulation, not a real phone.
The fix mutation was applied only in a throwaway copy of the tree; the worktree was not edited.
decisionsProposed: Fix F-M2-1 and add a test that runs a slow-load Play (strip shown), enters, exits and asserts focus is on Play, then re-submit for a short QA round (rerun stalestrip and mobile focus probes only, plus the shell and full suites).
lessonsProposed: A warm-only harness hides every slow-load path: always run one cycle where the strip is shown (hold the load past 400 ms) and assert focus after Exit, because state that is only set on the slow path (stripShownAt) can leak into the return path.

Log focusin and focusout around a transition instead of reading document.activeElement once; the two-step Play then Cancel then body sequence exposed a mount-time autofocus that a single read would call a harmless blur.
A pair-diff ratio around a swap needs the preceding camera motion removed before blaming the swap: here the 'swap spike' was the last fov step and the swap itself was quieter than its neighbours.
